During its early and mid-20th-century peak, VUC was one of the stronger clubs in Dutch football outside the absolute top powers. It competed in the highest amateur divisions and had notable success during wartime and post-war periods, including an important district championship in 1944. The club was known for attracting large crowds in its best years and even hosted matches featuring prominent players such as Bertus de Harder. It also played a role in Dutch football culture by serving as a training ground for the national team thanks to its early facilities.

In later decades, VUC moved away from the top national level as professional football developed in the Netherlands. It remained active as a strong amateur club in The Hague and continues today as a community-based organisation focused on youth development and lower-league competition. Although it no longer competes in professional football, VUC is still respected for its long history, its contribution to early Dutch football, and its continuing role in the local sporting landscape.

name: TSV LONGA
content:
TSV LONGA (Tilburgse Sportvereniging Lichaams Ontwikkeling Na Gedane Arbeid) was a historic football club from Tilburg in the Netherlands, founded in 1920. The club emerged from a sporting association linked to employees of a local bank and quickly developed into one of the important early football organisations in the city. LONGA became known for its white shirts and black shorts and grew into a major multi-team club within Brabant football during the amateur era. It played a key role in the development of football culture in Tilburg alongside other traditional clubs in the city.

During the interwar period, LONGA experienced its strongest sporting years. The club reached the top level of Dutch football and achieved notable success, including winning the KNVB Cup in 1926, one of the biggest achievements in its history. In the 1930s and 1940s, LONGA remained competitive at a high regional and national level and even reached the decisive stages of national competition in 1944. At its peak, the club played in front of large crowds at its Sportpark, which could hold up to 15,000 spectators.

After the introduction of professional football in the Netherlands in the 1950s, LONGA struggled to maintain top-level status and gradually moved between divisions. In 1965, the club left professional football and returned to amateur status, focusing again on local competition and community sport. Decades later, it eventually merged with other Tilburg clubs (including NOAD and RKTVV) to form a new unified club structure in the city. Today, LONGA is remembered as one of the traditional pioneers of Tilburg football, known for its early success, strong local identity, and contribution to Dutch football history.

name: SC Heerenveen
content:
SC Heerenveen is a professional football club from Heerenveen in the Netherlands, founded on 20 July 1920. The club originally began under different names and structures before eventually becoming SC Heerenveen in 1977 after the separation of amateur and professional sections. It is one of the most recognizable clubs in Dutch football outside the traditional “big three,” and is strongly associated with the province of Friesland, which gives it a distinct regional identity and fan culture.

For most of its modern history, Heerenveen has been a stable Eredivisie club, regularly competing at the top level of Dutch football since the early 1990s. The club is known for its attacking style, strong youth development, and ability to produce or develop talented players who later move to larger European teams. Its best league performances include finishing as runners-up in the late 1990s and qualifying multiple times for European competitions, including the UEFA Cup and Intertoto Cup campaigns.

One of the biggest achievements in the club’s history came in 2009, when SC Heerenveen won the KNVB Cup, securing its first major national trophy. The club also has a strong reputation for developing international players and maintaining a competitive squad despite not having the financial power of the top Dutch clubs. In recent years, Heerenveen has remained a consistent Eredivisie side, continuing to focus on stability, youth progression, and its distinctive Frisian identity within Dutch football.

name: Maurits
content:
Maurits was a Dutch football club from Geleen in the province of Limburg, founded on 15 June 1926. The club was originally created as the football team of the Staatsmijn Maurits (State Mine Maurits), which was one of the largest coal mines in the Netherlands. Because of this strong industrial connection, Maurits became closely linked with the mining community and represented the working-class culture of the region. The club played its home matches at the Mauritsstadion, which was built after World War II and became one of the notable stadiums in southern Dutch football.

During the 1940s and early 1950s, SV Maurits experienced its strongest period. The club reached the top level of Dutch football and even competed for the national championship in the late 1940s. Its best achievement came in the 1949–50 season, when Maurits won its regional division and took part in the national championship play-offs, finishing in a strong third place overall. The team was known for producing solid performances and for being one of the strongest representatives of Limburg football during that era, alongside other mining-based clubs.

In 1958, SV Maurits merged with the professional club Fortuna ’54, which marked the end of its independent existence as a football team. The merger was driven by financial and structural changes in Dutch football and helped create a stronger professional organisation in the region. After the merger, Maurits ceased to exist as a separate club, but its legacy remained important in Limburg football history. Today, it is remembered as a classic mining-era club that played a significant role in the development of Dutch football in the mid-20th century.

name: Hermes DVS
content:
Hermes DVS is a Dutch multi-sport club from Schiedam, founded on 8 April 1884, making it one of the oldest sports associations in the Netherlands. The club originally started as a cricket organisation under the name Hermes and later expanded to include football, becoming an important early representative of organised sport in the region. In 1919, Hermes merged with the football club DVS (Door Vereniging Sterk), which led to the formation of the modern Hermes DVS. The club developed a strong identity as a traditional community-based association combining different sports such as football, cricket, rugby, and squash.

In football, Hermes DVS was particularly prominent during the mid-20th century. The club competed at the highest levels of Dutch amateur football and reached its peak in the early professional era, including finishing as runners-up in the national championship in the 1951–52 season. It also played professional football from the introduction of professionalism in the 1950s until 1971, mainly in the second tier. During this period, Hermes produced several players who reached the national team and was considered a strong and respected club within Dutch football.

After leaving professional football in 1971, Hermes DVS returned to amateur status, where it continues today as a multi-sport club. Football remains an important part of its identity, but the club is now mainly focused on regional amateur competition and youth development. Despite no longer being part of the professional system, Hermes DVS is still recognised for its long history, its role in early Dutch football, and its broader sporting tradition in Schiedam.

name: USV Elinkwijk
content:
USV Elinkwijk is a Dutch football club from Utrecht, founded in 1919. It originally emerged from a workers’ sports association in the Elinkwijk district and developed into one of the most important clubs in the city’s early football history. The club became well known in the region for its strong community roots and for producing talented players from Utrecht’s working-class neighbourhoods. Its traditional identity is strongly connected with the blue-and-white colours and the historic Sportpark Zuilen.

Elinkwijk reached its sporting peak in the mid-20th century and became one of the notable Dutch clubs during the early professional era. It was one of the founding participants in the Eredivisie in 1956 and competed at the highest national level for several seasons in the late 1950s and 1960s. The club also produced several well-known players and contributed to Dutch football development during this period. However, like many smaller clubs, it struggled to maintain stability as professional football became more competitive.

In 1970, the professional branch of USV Elinkwijk merged with DOS and Velox to form FC Utrecht, which became the city’s main professional team. After the merger, Elinkwijk continued as an amateur club and still exists today in lower divisions of Dutch football. It remains active as a community-based organisation focused on local sport and youth development, and is still remembered for its important role in Utrecht’s football history and its contribution to the foundation of FC Utrecht.

name: Fortuna '54
content:
Fortuna ’54 was a Dutch football club from Geleen in the province of Limburg, founded on 1 June 1954. It is widely regarded as one of the most important pioneering clubs in the history of professional football in the Netherlands. The club was created by businessman Gied Joosten, who played a key role in introducing paid football in the country. Fortuna was built as a professional “glamour team,” attracting top Dutch and international players and immediately becoming a symbol of the new era of professional football.

In sporting terms, Fortuna ’54 quickly became one of the strongest teams in the Netherlands. The club was among the first participants in the professional competition and finished near the top of the league in its early years. Its greatest successes came in the KNVB Cup, which it won twice, in 1957 and 1964. During the late 1950s and early 1960s, Fortuna was known for its entertaining, attacking football and for assembling star-studded squads featuring well-known national team players.

Despite its sporting success, Fortuna ’54 struggled financially in the late 1960s as Dutch football became more structured and competitive. In 1968, the club merged with local rival Sittardia to form Fortuna Sittard (originally FSC), ending its existence as an independent team. Although Fortuna ’54 existed for only about 14 years, it remains a landmark club in Dutch football history, remembered as one of the pioneers that helped establish professional football in the Netherlands and shaped the modern game in Limburg.

name: VVV-Venlo
content:
VVV-Venlo is a Dutch professional football club from Venlo in the province of Limburg, founded on 7 February 1903. The club emerged from several early local football initiatives and gradually developed into one of the most established teams in the southern Netherlands. VVV is traditionally known as “The Good Old” and has a strong regional identity, with its home base at the distinctive De Koel stadium, which is built in a natural hollow and is famous for its steep stands and intense atmosphere.

Throughout its history, VVV-Venlo has mainly competed between the Eredivisie and Eerste Divisie, often moving between promotion and relegation. One of its most successful early periods came in the late 1950s, when the club won the KNVB Cup in 1959 and reached another final in 1962. In later decades, VVV became known as a resilient “yo-yo club,” regularly returning to the top flight despite limited resources. The club has also produced and hosted several notable players who later succeeded at higher levels of European football.

In modern times, VVV-Venlo continues to play an important role in Dutch football as a competitive second-tier or occasional Eredivisie side. It is strongly supported across North Limburg and maintains a reputation for community connection, talent development, and fighting spirit. While it has not established itself among the top Dutch clubs historically, VVV remains respected for its longevity, distinctive stadium, and consistent presence in professional football for over a century.

name: FC Groningen
content:
FC Groningen is a professional football club from Groningen in the Netherlands, founded on 16 June 1971 as the successor of GVAV. The club emerged after a restructuring of local football in the city, with GVAV itself tracing roots back to the early 20th century. FC Groningen quickly became the main representative of northern Dutch football and is strongly associated with its identity as “Trots van het Noorden” (Pride of the North). The club plays its home matches at the Euroborg stadium, which replaced the historic Oosterpark Stadion in the mid-2000s.

Since its foundation, Groningen has mostly competed in the Eredivisie and Eerste Divisie, often moving between promotion and relegation. The club achieved one of its best historical results in the 1990–91 season, when it finished third in the Eredivisie and qualified for European competitions. In 2015, FC Groningen won its first major trophy by securing the KNVB Cup, marking a key milestone in its modern history. The club is also known for its strong youth academy, which has produced several top-level players who went on to succeed in European football.

In European competition, FC Groningen has had several appearances since the 1980s, including notable UEFA Cup runs where it achieved surprising results against stronger international opponents. Over the decades, it has built a reputation as a well-organized, competitive club that can challenge higher-ranked teams on its day. Today, Groningen remains an important mid-to-upper level Dutch club, valued for its regional identity, talent development, and passionate support base in the north of the Netherlands.

name: FC Utrecht
content:
FC Utrecht is a professional football club from Utrecht in the Netherlands, founded on 1 July 1970. The club was created as a merger of three local teams—VV DOS, USV Elinkwijk, and Velox—in order to form a single strong representative for the city in professional football. Since its foundation, FC Utrecht has competed in the Eredivisie, the top tier of Dutch football, and plays its home matches at Stadion Galgenwaard, which is one of the most recognizable stadiums in the country.

In terms of sporting achievements, FC Utrecht is considered the strongest Dutch club outside the traditional “big three” (Ajax, PSV, Feyenoord). The club has won the KNVB Cup three times (1985, 2003, 2004) and also claimed the Johan Cruyff Shield in 2004. It has reached multiple European competitions and is known for occasional strong runs in UEFA tournaments, including group stage participation in the Europa League.

FC Utrecht is also notable for its consistency in top-flight football, as it has never been relegated from the Eredivisie since its formation. The club has built a reputation for developing young talent, maintaining a strong supporter culture, and being a competitive mid-to-upper table team in Dutch football. In modern seasons, Utrecht continues to aim for European qualification spots while remaining one of the most stable and respected clubs in the Netherlands outside the traditional elite.

name: Ajax Leiden
content:
Ajax Leiden was a Dutch football and cricket club from Leiden, founded on 1 June 1892. It was one of the early sporting associations in the Netherlands and played an important role in the development of football during the sport’s amateur beginnings. The club started as a multi-sport organization and quickly became known in the region of South Holland as one of the pioneering teams introducing structured football competition in the late 19th century. It was originally based in Leiden before later moving to Oegstgeest.

In the early years of Dutch football, Ajax Leiden competed in regional and national competitions and was part of the highest amateur divisions of its time. The club achieved some notable early success, including strong performances in the second tier and participation in early national competition structures. Like many clubs of that era, it helped shape the foundation of organized football in the Netherlands before the sport became fully professional. One of its notable contributions was developing players who later participated in early Dutch national team setups.

In 1918, Ajax Leiden merged with another club, De Sportman, to form ASC (Ajax Sportman Combinatie). This merger marked the end of Ajax Leiden as an independent club. Although it no longer exists, it remains historically significant as one of the early football clubs that helped establish the game in the Netherlands, especially in the Leiden region, and contributed to the formation of later sporting institutions in Dutch football history.

name: DSV Concordia
content:
DSV Concordia is a historic Dutch multi-sport club from Delft, founded on 15 October 1885, making it one of the oldest sports organisations in the Netherlands. The club originally started as a cricket association and later expanded into football, tennis, and golf, becoming an early example of a traditional “omni-sport” club. Football quickly became one of its main activities, and Concordia played an important role in the early development of Dutch football during the amateur era.

In football, DSV Concordia was one of the stronger early clubs in the Netherlands and achieved notable success in the pre-professional period. The club won the KNVB Cup in 1906 and was considered a competitive side in the top amateur competitions of the early 20th century. During this era, Concordia contributed to shaping Dutch football culture and also produced players who reached the national team, including Jan Thomée, one of the early Dutch international stars.

Over time, Concordia moved away from top-level football as the Dutch game became professional in the mid-20th century. Instead of joining the professional structure, the club remained an amateur organisation and gradually focused more on recreational sport and community activities. Today, DSV Concordia still exists in Delft as a multi-sport club, mainly active in amateur football and other sports, and is remembered for its long history and early contribution to Dutch football development.

name: DFC Dordrecht
content:
DFC (Dordrechtse Football Club) is one of the oldest football clubs in the Netherlands, founded on 16 August 1883 in the city of Dordrecht. Originally established as a cricket club before adding football, DFC became one of the early pioneers of organized Dutch football during the amateur era. The club played an important role in the development of the sport in the Netherlands and was among the founding institutions that helped shape the early national competition structure. Its traditional red-and-white colours became closely associated with football in Dordrecht.

During the first half of the 20th century, DFC achieved considerable success in Dutch football. The club won the KNVB Cup twice, in 1914 and 1932, and regularly competed at the highest national level before professionalism was introduced. DFC was also known for its strong football culture and attracted influential figures, including legendary English coach Jimmy Hogan, who briefly worked at the club and helped introduce more modern tactical ideas to Dutch football. In the late 1930s and early 1940s, the team also enjoyed strong league performances under coach Árpád Weisz.

After professional football arrived in the Netherlands in 1954, DFC continued as a professional club until 1972, when the professional and amateur branches separated. The professional section eventually evolved into what is now FC Dordrecht, while DFC remained an amateur club. Over time, the club moved away from the top levels of Dutch football but continued to exist as a traditional community-based side in Dordrecht. Today, DFC is remembered as one of the historic founding clubs of Dutch football and an important contributor to the sport’s early development in the country.

name: VSV Velsen
content:
VSV (Velseroorder Sport Vereniging) is a historic Dutch football club from the IJmuiden and Velsen region, officially founded in 1912. The club originally began under the name Unitas before adopting the VSV identity when it entered organized competition. As one of the oldest football clubs in the IJmond area, VSV played an important role in the development of football in North Holland and became closely connected to the sporting culture of the region. The club traditionally wore red-and-white colours and built a strong local following over the decades.

VSV achieved some of its greatest successes during the amateur and early professional eras of Dutch football. The club won the KNVB Cup in 1938 after defeating AGOVV in the final, which remains one of the biggest achievements in its history. After professional football was introduced in the Netherlands in the 1950s, VSV joined the professional leagues and spent several seasons mainly in the Eerste Divisie. In 1963, the club won the Tweede Divisie title and earned promotion, confirming its status as one of the stronger regional sides outside the traditional Dutch elite.

In the same year, the professional sections of VSV and Stormvogels merged to create SC Telstar, a new professional club representing the Velsen area. While the professional branch disappeared into Telstar, VSV itself continued independently as an amateur club. Today, the club remains active in lower amateur divisions and continues to preserve its long history and local traditions. VSV is still remembered as an important part of Dutch football heritage, particularly for its cup success and its contribution to the creation of Telstar.

name: CVV Rotterdam
content:
Charloisse Voetbalvereniging, commonly known as CVV, was a historic Dutch football club founded in 1908 in the Charlois district of Rotterdam. Originally established under the name Excelsior, the club later changed its name to avoid confusion with another Rotterdam side. CVV quickly became one of the notable amateur football clubs in the Netherlands, developing a reputation for strong performances and a loyal local following.

The club achieved national recognition in 1920 when it won the Dutch KNVB Cup, an impressive accomplishment for a non-professional side at the time. Throughout its history, CVV spent many years competing in the higher amateur divisions and enjoyed several successful periods, including national amateur championships in the 1960s and 1970s. The club was also known for producing talented players and maintaining a strong football culture within Rotterdam.

In 2001, CVV merged with another local club to form CVV-Mercurius as part of efforts to keep football alive in the area. Eventually, further mergers led to the creation of newer football organizations, bringing the original CVV era to an end. Despite no longer existing as an independent club, CVV remains an important part of Rotterdam football history and is remembered for its traditions, achievements, and contribution to Dutch amateur football.

name: VV Schoten
content:
VV Schoten is a Dutch amateur football club based in Haarlem, in the province of North Holland. Founded in 1910, the club has a long-standing tradition within Dutch amateur football and is considered one of the historic local clubs in the Haarlem region. The team plays its home matches at Sportpark Vergierdeweg and is known for its yellow and black club colors.

Throughout its history, VV Schoten has competed mainly in the Dutch amateur football system and developed a reputation as a community-focused club with strong local support. The organization offers teams for various age groups, including youth, senior, and recreational football, helping to develop local talent and encourage participation in the sport. The club has remained an important part of Haarlem’s sporting culture for more than a century.

Besides its competitive activities, VV Schoten is recognized for its welcoming atmosphere and active club life. Over the years, it has hosted football tournaments and community events that strengthen its connection with players, families, and supporters. Although it has never been among the biggest professional clubs in the Netherlands, VV Schoten continues to play an important role in preserving the tradition and spirit of amateur football in Dutch society.

name: RFC Rotterdam
content:
RFC Rotterdam, officially known as Rotterdamsche Football Club, was a Dutch football club based in Rotterdam. The club was founded in 1904, originally under the name Olympia, before adopting the RFC name a few years later. Throughout much of its existence, RFC competed in the Dutch amateur football system and became one of the recognized traditional clubs in Rotterdam’s football scene.

During the early decades of Dutch football, RFC achieved several promotions and spent periods playing in higher regional divisions. The club was known for its green-and-white colors and played its matches at grounds near the Essenburgsingel area of Rotterdam. RFC also contributed players to Dutch football at a national level, including Daaf Drok, who represented the Netherlands in the 1930s.

Although RFC never became one of the dominant professional clubs in the Netherlands, it maintained a respected place within Rotterdam football history for many decades. Financial and organizational difficulties eventually led to the club’s decline, and RFC ceased to exist in 1997 after more than 90 years of activity. Even after its disappearance, the club is still remembered by football historians and former supporters as part of Rotterdam’s rich football heritage.

name: ZFC Zaandam
content:
ZFC, short for Zaanlandsche Football Club, was a historic football club from Zaandam in the Netherlands. Founded in 1904, the club became one of the most recognized teams in the Zaan region and played an important role in Dutch football during the early and mid-20th century. The club originally emerged from a merger between smaller local teams and quickly established itself within regional competitions.

During its most successful years, ZFC competed in the highest levels of Dutch football and won the KNVB Cup in the 1924–25 season. The club was known for its distinctive red-and-white checkered shirts and attracted strong local support in Zaandam. In the 1930s, ZFC regularly challenged major Dutch clubs and produced several talented players who represented national teams or became well-known figures in Dutch football history.

After the introduction of professional football in the Netherlands during the 1950s, ZFC joined the professional leagues and spent years competing in the Eerste Divisie and Tweede Divisie. However, financial difficulties and declining attendance eventually weakened the club’s position. In 1990, ZFC merged with another local side, ZVV, to form Hellas Sport Combinatie, bringing the independent history of ZFC to an end. Even today, the club is remembered as an important symbol of football tradition in the Zaan region.

name: XerxesDZB
content:
XerxesDZB is a Dutch amateur football club based in Rotterdam, formed in 2000 through the merger of two historic clubs, Xerxes and DZB. The club continues the football traditions of both organizations and has become a well-known name in Rotterdam amateur football. Xerxes itself had a long history dating back to 1904 and was one of the older football clubs in the Netherlands, while DZB also had a strong local reputation within Rotterdam’s sporting community.

The club plays its home matches at Sportpark Faas Wilkes, named after the legendary Dutch footballer who once played for Xerxes. Throughout its history, XerxesDZB has competed mainly in the Dutch amateur leagues and has earned recognition for developing talented players and maintaining a strong youth academy. The club’s black-and-white colors and traditional identity have remained important symbols for supporters and former members of the original clubs.

Besides its sporting activities, XerxesDZB is known for its strong community involvement and focus on youth development. The organization provides football opportunities for players of all ages and works to promote teamwork, discipline, and local engagement through sport. Although it is not part of professional Dutch football, XerxesDZB continues to play an important role in preserving Rotterdam’s football heritage and amateur football culture.

name: PEC Zwolle
content:
PEC Zwolle is a professional football club based in Zwolle, a city in the northeastern Netherlands. The club was originally founded in 1910 as PH EDN and later became known as PEC Zwolle after several mergers and name changes throughout its history. PEC stands for “Prins Hendrik Ende Desespereert Nimmer Combinatie,” reflecting the union of local football organizations. The club has become one of the most recognized football teams outside the traditional Dutch football powers.

Throughout its history, PEC Zwolle has competed in both the Eredivisie and Eerste Divisie, experiencing periods of promotion and relegation. The club achieved one of its greatest successes in 2014 when it won the KNVB Cup by defeating Ajax 5–1 in the final, a historic result that brought national attention to Zwolle. That same year, the club also won the Johan Cruyff Shield, marking the most successful period in its modern history. PEC Zwolle plays its home matches at the MAC³PARK Stadion and is known for its passionate supporters and strong local identity.

In addition to its first-team achievements, PEC Zwolle is respected for its youth development and commitment to community football. The club has produced and developed several talented Dutch players over the years and continues to invest in its academy structure. Despite operating with a smaller budget compared to the biggest Dutch clubs, PEC Zwolle remains competitive and plays an important role in Dutch professional football through its traditions, fan culture, and long football heritage.

name: Excelsior
content:
Excelsior Rotterdam is a professional football club from Rotterdam, Netherlands, founded in 1902. Officially known as Rotterdamse Voetbal en Atletiek Vereniging Excelsior, the club is one of the oldest football organizations in the country. Excelsior has traditionally been recognized as a smaller but respected club within Dutch football, often competing alongside the larger Rotterdam teams such as Feyenoord and Sparta Rotterdam. The club plays its home matches at Van Donge & De Roo Stadion and is known for its black-and-red colors.

Throughout its history, Excelsior has mainly competed between the Eredivisie and Eerste Divisie, earning a reputation as a competitive and well-organized club. One of the club’s greatest strengths has been youth development, with many talented Dutch players starting their careers in Rotterdam before moving to bigger European clubs. Excelsior has also maintained a close cooperation with Feyenoord for many years, which helped strengthen its player development system and football structure.

Despite having a smaller budget compared to the major Dutch clubs, Excelsior has remained an important part of professional football in the Netherlands. The club is admired for its attacking style of play, community atmosphere, and ability to compete against stronger opponents. Over the decades, Excelsior Rotterdam has become a symbol of determination and stability in Dutch football, maintaining its place within the country’s rich sporting tradition.

name: HVV Helmond
content:
HVV Helmond was a Dutch football club based in the city of Helmond in the province of North Brabant. The club was founded in 1912 and became one of the important local football organizations in the region during the early decades of Dutch football. HVV Helmond competed mainly in amateur competitions and built a strong reputation through its long football tradition and community involvement.

Throughout its history, the club developed a loyal local following and contributed to the growth of football culture in Helmond. HVV Helmond played its matches in the traditional club colors of black and white and was known for promoting sportsmanship and youth participation. Like many historical Dutch football clubs, it experienced both successful periods and difficult seasons while competing against regional rivals.

In 1967, HVV Helmond merged with another local club, Helmondia ’55, to create what is now known as Helmond Sport. This merger allowed professional football in Helmond to continue under a stronger and more unified organization. Although HVV Helmond no longer exists as an independent club, its history remains an important part of the football heritage of the city and Dutch amateur football tradition.

name: RFC Roermond
content:

The club was founded in 1910 and became one of the notable football organizations in the southern Netherlands during the early years of Dutch football. RFC stood for Roermondse Football Club, and the team developed a strong local identity through its participation in regional and national amateur competitions.

Throughout its history, RFC Roermond was known for its commitment to community football and youth development. The club competed mainly in the amateur leagues but earned respect for its organized structure and competitive spirit. In later years, the club experienced organizational and financial challenges that affected its long-term stability. Former players and supporters still remember the club as one of the classic football institutions of Limburg and an important contributor to local football tradition.

name: WVV Wageningen
content:

Founded in 1911, the club became well known within Dutch football for its long tradition and competitive performances in both amateur and professional leagues. WVV stood for Wageningse Voetbal Vereniging, and the club played an important role in the sporting culture of the city for many decades.

During its most successful years, WVV Wageningen competed in the Eerste Divisie and occasionally challenged stronger Dutch clubs in national competitions. The team was especially respected during the 1970s and 1980s, when it built a reputation for disciplined football and strong team spirit. The club played its home matches at Stadion De Wageningse Berg, a stadium that became closely associated with football history in Wageningen and attracted loyal local supporters.

Despite its tradition and popularity, WVV Wageningen eventually faced serious financial difficulties that affected the club’s future. In 1992, the professional football organization went bankrupt and disappeared from the Dutch professional leagues. Although the club no longer exists in its original form, WVV Wageningen remains remembered as an important part of Dutch football heritage and as one of the classic smaller clubs that contributed to the development of football in the Netherlands.

name: RKSV Groene Ster
content:

The club was founded in 1922 and has become one of the most recognized amateur football organizations in southern Netherlands. The name “Groene Ster,” meaning “Green Star,” reflects the club’s traditional green-and-white colors, which have remained an important part of its identity throughout its history.

Over the decades, RKSV Groene Ster has competed in various levels of Dutch amateur football and built a strong reputation for competitive performances and youth development. The club achieved national attention in the KNVB Cup on several occasions, especially when facing professional teams from higher divisions. Groene Ster is known for its passionate supporters and strong connection to the local community, making it an important sporting institution in the Limburg region.

Besides its achievements on the pitch, the club has focused heavily on developing young players and promoting football at the community level. RKSV Groene Ster offers teams for different age groups and continues to encourage participation in sport among local residents. Although it remains an amateur club, Groene Ster has earned respect across Dutch football for its tradition, organization, and contribution to football culture in the Netherlands.

name: DWV Amsterdam
content:

The club was founded in 1908, and its name stands for “Door Wilskracht Verkregen,” which can be translated as “Achieved Through Willpower.” Throughout its long history, D.W.V. has been known as one of the traditional football clubs in Amsterdam, developing a strong local identity and maintaining an important place within Dutch amateur football.

The club has spent most of its existence competing in regional and amateur leagues, where it built a reputation for discipline, teamwork, and youth development. D.W.V. plays its home matches in Amsterdam-Noord and is recognized for its black-and-white club colors. Over the decades, many local players developed their football skills within the club’s youth system, helping D.W.V. remain an active and respected football organization in the Dutch capital.

name: SC Helmondia
content:

name: FC Volendam
content:
FC Volendam is a Dutch professional football club based in Volendam, a fishing village in the province of North Holland. The club was originally founded in 1920 under the name Victoria and later became RKSV Volendam before adopting its current professional structure as FC Volendam in 1977. It represents one of the most recognizable clubs in Dutch football outside the major cities, strongly connected to its local community and identity.

Throughout its history, FC Volendam has been known as a classic “yo-yo club” because of its frequent promotions and relegations between the Eredivisie and Eerste Divisie. The club has achieved a record number of promotions to the top division and is widely respected for its ability to develop talented young players who often move on to bigger Dutch and European teams. Its home matches are played at the Kras Stadion, a compact ground known for its close and passionate atmosphere.

Despite limited financial resources compared to top Dutch clubs, Volendam has maintained a strong footballing identity based on attacking play, local talent, and community support. The club has also reached several notable achievements, including appearances in national cup finals, though it has never won the top domestic league. Over the years, FC Volendam has become a symbol of resilience in Dutch football, continuously bouncing back between divisions while maintaining a loyal fan base and strong village connection.

name: DHC Delft
content:
DHC Delft (Delfia Hollandia Combinatie) is a Dutch football club based in Delft, founded in 1910. It is one of the traditional clubs in the city and has a long history in Dutch football, mainly at amateur level. The club plays at Sportpark Brasserskade and is known for its black-and-green colours and strong local identity. It developed as a result of a merger between earlier Delft football organizations and quickly became an important part of the city’s sporting culture.

Between 1955 and 1968, DHC also played professional football in the Netherlands. During this period, the club competed in the Eerste Divisie and Tweede Divisie, experiencing both moderate success and financial challenges. In 1967, DHC’s professional branch merged with the Rotterdam club Xerxes, forming a short-lived combined team known as Xerxes/DHC. This project lasted only a short time due to financial instability, and it marked the end of DHC’s professional era.

After the collapse of professional football activities, DHC continued as an amateur club in Delft. It rebuilt its identity around local football, youth development, and community involvement. Over time, the club returned to the lower tiers of Dutch amateur football, where it still competes today. Despite no longer being a professional side, DHC remains an important historical club in Dutch football, known for its long tradition and contribution to the sport in Delft.

name: Fortuna Sittard
content:

The club was formed in 1968 through the merger of Fortuna 54 and Sittardia, two local teams that combined to strengthen football in the region. Fortuna 54 had previously been one of the pioneers of professional football in the Netherlands, while Sittardia brought a strong local amateur tradition. Together, they created a club that represents the city of Sittard and the wider Limburg area.

Throughout its history, Fortuna Sittard has experienced a mix of success and financial difficulty. The club has played many seasons in the Eredivisie, especially during the 1980s and 1990s, and has also spent time in the Eerste Divisie. It is known for developing talented players such as Mark van Bommel, Fernando Ricksen, and Kevin Hofland, who later became important figures in Dutch and international football. The team plays its home matches at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion, which has been its base since the late 1990s.

Despite periods of instability, including serious financial problems and relegations, Fortuna Sittard has managed to survive and rebuild several times. In recent years, the club has returned to the Eredivisie and worked toward becoming more stable both on and off the pitch. Today, Fortuna is seen as a resilient club with a strong regional identity, known for its passionate supporters and its ability to develop and showcase young talent in Dutch football.

name: Helmond Sport
content:

Helmond Sport quickly established itself in the Dutch football system and has mainly competed in the Eerste Divisie, the second tier of Dutch football. The team plays its home matches at the GS Staalwerken Stadion and is known for its red and black colours.

One of the most successful periods in the club’s history came in the early 1980s. In 1982, Helmond Sport won the Eerste Divisie championship and earned promotion to the Eredivisie for the first time. Although the club managed to stay in the top division for a short period, it was soon relegated back to the second tier. A major highlight followed in 1985, when Helmond Sport reached the KNVB Cup final, where they narrowly lost to FC Utrecht.

Since then, Helmond Sport has remained a stable but modest club in Dutch professional football, often competing in the middle or lower parts of the Eerste Divisie. Despite not returning to the Eredivisie for long periods, the club is respected for its resilience, youth development, and strong regional identity. It continues to play an important role in Helmond’s sporting culture and maintains a loyal local fan base.

name: RBC Roosendaal
content:
RBC Roosendaal is a Dutch football club from the city of Roosendaal in the province of North Brabant. The club was founded in 1912 under the name Excelsior and later went through several name changes and mergers before becoming Roosendaal Boys Combinatie (RBC). Over time, it developed into one of the more notable football clubs in the region, with a strong local identity and long-standing presence in Dutch football.

The club became professional in 1955 and spent many years moving between divisions in the Dutch football system. One of its biggest achievements came in the early 2000s, when RBC reached the Eredivisie, the top level of Dutch football, and competed there for several seasons. The team also reached the KNVB Cup final in 1986, which remains one of the highlights in its history. Its home matches were played at the RBC Stadion in Roosendaal.

Despite its sporting moments of success, the club faced serious financial problems later on. In 2011, RBC Roosendaal went bankrupt and lost its professional status, effectively ending its existence as a professional club. It later restarted as an amateur team and began rebuilding from the lower divisions. Today, RBC is remembered as a club with a rich but turbulent history, known for its resilience and contribution to Dutch football culture.
